messages.author: 5973acf80afe16c7
messages.subject: Planning road survey
parts:
Hello. I am new to distance sampling and trying to design a survey for counting herbivores on a game reserve. We have to use the existing road network on the reserve for our counts which means we can't do parallel-line transects. I've been trying to find information on how to plan a road-based survey but having trouble coming up with anything.

I am wondering whether it's better to have 1 long transect that runs across the whole reserve (in which case how to I plan the route to take?) or whether we should make up a number of 200m transects randomly distributed over the reserve and incorporate them into a route, so we only count the animals when we are on those 200m sections of road.

A couple of other things I wondered:

- Is it better to avoid using fenceline roads, as when on the fenceline we can only get animals on one side of us and that might affect the results?
- Roads are not dead-straight lines. Will this have a detrimental impact on the data?

Sorry for the novice questions, and thanks for any advice

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Planning road survey
parts:
Road surveys:

The purpose of a survey design is the create a *random* sample of your study area such that you can have confidence in the assumption that the places you sampled with your transects are representative of the area to which you wish to make inference.  By definition, roads are not placed randomly on the landscape, hence it is contradictory to "design" a road survey.  That is the reason you are unable to find information regarding this subject.  It would be best to not use roads for your sampling.

Animals know where roads are located and the either avoid roads or are attracted to them; in either case, this interferes with your ability to make sound inference from surveys that are road based.

A better strategy is to define the area about which you wish to make inference, then use the Distance software or some other random process to place transects into that area.  It is best to have more short transects than a small number of short transects.  You need replicates across the study area to have more confidence in your results.

Feel free to ask additional questions.
